name: CONSORT 2025
source: Hopewell S, Chan AW, Collins GS, Hrobjartsson A, Moher D, Schulz KF, et al. CONSORT 2025 Statement: updated guideline for reporting randomised trials. BMJ. 2025;388:e081123 / PLoS Med. 2025. https://www.consort-statement.org/

items.text: Identify the study as a randomised trial in the title.
Provide a structured summary of trial design, methods, results, and conclusions.
Name the trial registry, registration number, and date of registration.
State where the full trial protocol and statistical analysis plan can be accessed.
State whether and where de-identified participant data, analytical code, and research materials can be accessed.
Report sources of funding and the role of funders, and state financial and other conflicts of interest.
Explain the scientific background, rationale, and medical evidence gap.
State specific objectives or pre-specified hypotheses concerning benefits and harms.
Describe how patients and the public were involved in the trial design, conduct, and reporting.
Describe the trial design (such as parallel or crossover), allocation ratio, and framework (superiority or non-inferiority).
Describe any important changes to methods or design after trial commencement, with reasons.
Describe settings and locations where the trial was conducted and data were collected.
State eligibility criteria for participants, and where applicable, criteria for sites and intervention providers.
Provide details of the interventions and comparators to permit replication, including administration and timing.
Define pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes, measurement instruments, metrics, and assessment time points.
Describe methods used to define, collect, and assess adverse events and unintended harms.
Explain how sample size was determined, including clinical assumptions, effect sizes, and interim analysis stopping rules.
Describe method used to generate the random sequence, including block sizes, stratification, and restriction.
Describe mechanism used to conceal allocation sequence (such as central randomisation or sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes).
Specify who generated the allocation sequence, who enrolled participants, and who assigned participants to interventions.
Describe who was blinded after assignment to interventions (participants, care providers, outcome assessors, data analysts), and how.
Describe statistical methods used to compare groups for primary and secondary outcomes, handling of missing data, and non-adherence analyses.
Report participant flow through each stage (assessed, excluded, randomised, received intervention, lost to follow-up, and analysed), ideally via flow diagram.
Report recruitment and follow-up dates, whether the trial stopped early, and baseline clinical and demographic characteristics of each group.
For each primary and secondary outcome, report number of participants analysed per group, effect size, and precision (confidence interval).
Report all important adverse events, harms, or unintended effects in each group.
Report results of any subgroup, interaction, or sensitivity analyses, distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory analyses.
Provide interpretation consistent with results, balancing benefits and harms, and considering other relevant evidence.
Discuss trial limitations addressing potential sources of bias, imprecision, multiplicity, and generalisability.
Report details of trial monitoring, data monitoring committee (DSMB), ethics committee approvals, and protocol compliance.
